title: Lesson 14: Testing and Verification: Proving It Works Before You Claim It Does
description: Proving agent work by watching tool calls fire, reading real output and exit codes instead of trusting prose, verifying the result in the system, and building a repeatable gate so the work stays proven.

questions.question: An agent reports that it updated a record. What does this statement represent?
options: A claim, which is not proof until the record itself is read back and checked
A verified result, because the agent says it completed the task it described
A repeatable gate, because the same update could be applied again later on
A tool trace, because the agent has named the specific action it performed
questions.explanation: What the agent says is a claim, and only reading the result back in the system turns that claim into evidence.

questions.question: A command is run through a terminal tool. Which evidence tells you whether it actually succeeded?
options: The sentence the agent writes summarizing what the command did
The agent stating that the command completed without any errors
The command's actual output and its exit code
The length of time the command took to finish running
questions.explanation: The tool's real output and exit code are the evidence; a summary sentence about the command is not proof that it ran correctly.

questions.question: Watching a tool fire proves the agent tried. What does it take to prove the result is correct?
options: A second run that produces output of roughly the same length as the original run did
Reading the result back in the system and comparing it against the source
An exit code of zero from the command that produced the reported result
A clean diff showing that the intended file on disk was modified as planned
questions.explanation: Effort is not correctness, so the result is verified in the system against the source the way the client's team would use it.
